name_note: The genomes GTDB places in g__Haemophilus_D are labelled Haemophilus in NCBI; the GTDB suffix _D marks a split of the classical genus, so this taxon is narrower than Haemophilus in the literature.

sentences.text: Haemophilus is a bacterial genus of the human mouth; a 16S rRNA survey of 59 healthy, non-smoking women in their twenties listed it among the dominant oral genera at 10.1 percent.
In that survey Haemophilus was also among the taxa discriminating tongue coating from the other sampled oral sites.
A harmonized re-analysis of five longitudinal paediatric cohorts reported oral succession from Streptococcus and Staphylococcus to Haemophilus, Neisseria and Veillonella.

A perspective on chronic airway diseases describes neutrophilic airways as predominated by the phylum Proteobacteria and the genus Haemophilus, with neutrophil elastase impairing mucociliary clearance.
